An explicit compactly supported Gibbs equilibrium satisfies the required mass, momentum, and tensor second-moment conditions. We derive the quasilinear formulation and characteristic speeds, establish the continuous mechanical-energy balance with geometric work and frictional dissipation, and obtain a weak entropy inequality for vanishing-viscosity limits under stated convergence assumptions. On the rotating sphere with a fixed round metric, the skew-adjoint force represents Coriolis effects. We construct a kinetic finite-volume scheme combining local fluxes, hydrostatic reconstruction, and geometric source terms. A second-order time integrator uses independently restricted steps at its two Euler stages. The scheme conserves discrete water volume, preserves nonnegative depth under a sufficient CFL condition, and is well balanced for lakes at rest, including wet/dry interfaces. Six-hour simulations of a localized surface disturbance over Earth topography with Manning bottom friction maintain positive depths and conserve water volume to near machine precision. Comparison with a spherical central-upwind method shows similar surface-wave propagation and gauge time series, with remaining differences in late-time local extrema.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo Hern\'andez-Due\~nas

item.title: Recovering Small Perturbations of a Known Inclusion from One Mixed Steklov Eigenpair with Local Boundary Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.16596v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the recovery of small normal displacements of a known inclusion from a single mixed Steklov eigenpair. The data consist of the eigenvalue and the eigenfunction trace on any nonempty open subset of the fixed outer boundary, with the eigenfunction normalized using only that subset. For an inner Dirichlet condition, we prove that the linearized measurement map is injective at every simple eigenvalue. A compatible adjoint identity yields a reconstruction method with a conditional stability estimate on any fixed finite-dimensional space of smooth displacements. For the principal Dirichlet eigenpair, the same local data also determine the inclusion uniquely among sufficiently small normal graphs. In a three-dimensional concentric shell, the eigenvalue determines the mean displacement at first order, while spherical harmonics diagonalize the remaining full-boundary trace map. The singular values decay exponentially with harmonic degree, yielding logarithmic conditional stability under a Sobolev prior. Numerical experiments using the perturbed geometry illustrate the quadratic linearization error and the deterioration of conditioning as the observed patch shrinks. For an inner Neumann condition, we prove linearized injectivity at every positive simple eigenvalue.
item.dc:creator: Jiho Hong

item.title: Access to the quasi-geostrophic model from within the BK19 compressible flow solver
item.description: arXiv:2611.16601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend BK19 the semi-implicit finite-volume solver, to provide access to the quasi-geostrophic (QG) regime within the same compressible framework that already admits soundproof and hydrostatic limits. In order to achieve this goal, we incorporate the asymptotic framework from the continuous theory into the numerical scheme. Adopting the usual asymptotic setting for the quasi-geostrophic regime and using it directly in the numerical model, we perform a scale analysis of the compressible Euler equations in the synoptic length and time scales in the limit of small Rossby number. In this limit, the discrete implicit step recovers geostrophic balance, together with the pseudo-incompressible divergence constraint. We construct a staggered-grid curl operator consistent with the discrete derivatives and use it to define the vorticity in the numerical framework. An asymptotic analysis of the fully discrete scheme then yields a Poisson-type equation for the leading-order Exner-pressure perturbation that coincides with the QG pressure Poisson equation in the continuous theory. As a result of this analysis, we introduce two additional blending switches that (i) convert the elliptic pressure problem from the full Helmholtz to its QG Poisson-type equation and (ii) control whether the horizontal momenta are updated prognostically or diagnosed from geostrophic balance. In combination with the existing soundproof and hydrostatic switches, the resulting algorithm can be operated in fully compressible, pseudo-incompressible, hydrostatic, and QG modes without changing the underlying discretization. The functionality of the numerical scheme in the QG regime is then tested by two idealized vortex test cases to show how stable the vortices remain in the QG run and that, as the Rossby number is reduced, the full compressible scheme converges to slow, balanced QG dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Amir Maghoul, Rupert Klein

item.title: A posteriori error estimates for fully coupled McKean-Vlasov FBSDEs with jumps
item.description: arXiv:2611.17087v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a two-sided a posteriori error estimate for numerical approximations of fully coupled McKean-Vlasov forward-backward SDEs with jumps under full-tuple law dependence. The coefficients may depend on the joint law of $(X,Y,Z,U)$, and we allow infinite jump activity. We construct a computable estimator ${\mathcal{E}_\pi}$ for the squared full-tuple error ${\mathcal{D}_\pi}$ relative to the exact Euler solution. The estimator uses the boundary and cumulative residuals of any admissible grid approximation. Under monotonicity and on sufficiently fine grids, $c\,{\mathcal{E}_\pi} \le {\mathcal{D}_\pi} \le C\,{\mathcal{E}_\pi}$. The efficiency bound holds without monotonicity or a mesh restriction. Analogous two-sided bounds hold for the continuous-time error up to a discretisation remainder that vanishes under coefficient time regularity. Closed-form and state-nonlinear benchmarks cover full-tuple law dependence, mark-dependent jump integrands, nonzero orthogonal martingales and infinite jump activity. In our experiments, the estimator tracks the discrete error during neural training and across Picard iterations. In a mean-field inventory model, we use the estimator and a computable discretisation term to bound the excess cost of the computed control over the discrete optimum.
item.dc:creator: Chunrong Feng, Christian Garry

item.title: Convergence rates for smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) with nonlinear pressure
item.description: arXiv:2611.17151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish quantitative convergence results for the smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) method approximating the compressible Euler equations with nonlinear pressure laws $\rho^\gamma$, $\gamma\geq 2$. Our approach is based on a nonlocal approximation of the pressure force that preserves the energy structure of the original system, including an exact energy balance. Using the relative entropy method, we prove convergence towards smooth solutions of the compressible Euler equations as the nonlocality parameter $\varepsilon\to0$, with algebraic convergence rates and an explicit algebraic relationship between $\varepsilon$ and the number of particles $N$. In particular, we obtain quantitative convergence rates for the density in the Wasserstein distance and negative Sobolev norms, and for the momentum in the flat metric. A key feature of our analysis is that it applies to measure-valued densities in the nonlocal system, providing a unified framework for both continuum and particle solutions. Our results extend the existing rigorous convergence theory for SPH beyond quadratic pressure ($\gamma=2$) to general nonlinear pressure laws with $\gamma\geq 2$ on the periodic domain.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Gwiazda, Jakub Skrzeczkowski, Jakub Wo\'znicki

item.title: Iterative Refinement of A Modified Lavrentiev Regularization Method for De-convolution of the Discrete Helmholtz Type Differential Filter
item.description: arXiv:1801.08913v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze an iterated, modified Lavrentiev regularization method (Mitlar) for deconvolving the Helmholtz-type differential filter $G=(I-\delta^2\Delta)^{-1}$ used in large eddy simulation. The method replaces the Lavrentiev operator $G+\alpha I$ by the convex combination $(1-\alpha)G+\alpha I$; each step costs one Helmholtz solve, exactly as in iterated Lavrentiev regularization. We show that this one-line change has a precise structural meaning: the regularized operator is again a Helmholtz filter, now with the smaller radius $\sqrt{\alpha}\,\delta$, and $J$ refinement steps coincide with van Cittert approximate deconvolution of order $J$ applied to that filter. Consequently the regularization error is governed by the product $\alpha\delta^2$ rather than by $\alpha$ alone. We prove sharp error bounds of order $(\alpha\delta^2)^{s}$ on a Hilbert scale, $0\le s\le J+1$, with saturation exactly at $s=J+1$; show that for noise-free data the Mitlar error never exceeds the iterated Lavrentiev error, for every datum, every $\alpha$ and every $J$; give a priori parameter choices for noisy data with explicit $\delta$-dependence; and prove finite element error bounds whose constants grow only linearly in $J$. Finally we show that the iterates decrease a natural energy functional for every $\alpha>0$, and derive a computable stopping rule that guarantees monotone decrease of a weighted error and always terminates. Numerical examples illustrate the theory and compare Mitlar with a family of Tikhonov--Lavrentiev methods.
item.dc:creator: Nathaniel Mays, Ming Zhong

item.title: A hybrid FEM-PINN method for time-dependent partial differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2409.02810v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we present a hybrid numerical method for solving evolution partial differential equations (PDEs) by merging the time finite element method with deep neural networks. In contrast to the conventional deep learning-based formulation where the neural network is defined on a spatiotemporal domain, our methodology utilizes finite element basis functions in the time direction where the space-dependent coefficients are defined as the output of a neural network. We then apply the Galerkin or collocation projection in the time direction to obtain a system of PDEs for the space-dependent coefficients which is approximated in the framework of PINN. The advantages of such a hybrid formulation are twofold: statistical errors are avoided for the integral in the time direction, and the neural network's output can be regarded as a set of reduced spatial basis functions. To further alleviate the difficulties from high dimensionality and low regularity, we have developed an adaptive sampling strategy that refines the training set. More specifically, we use an explicit density model to approximate the distribution induced by the PDE residual and then augment the training set with new time-dependent random samples given by the learned density model. The effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed method have been demonstrated through a series of numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Xiaodong Feng, Haojiong Shangguan, Tao Tang, Xiaoliang Wan

item.title: Interface Energy and Phase Transformations: A Comparative Analysis of Cahn-Hilliard and CALPHAD-based Models in Ternary Substitutional Alloys
item.description: arXiv:2411.16430v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Diffusional phase transformations in alloys are modeled either by phase-field methods of Cahn-Hilliard type, in which a double-well free energy and a gradient term impose an interface energy, or by reactive diffusion models, in which the driving forces follow from the CALPHAD methodology, the convex hull of the molar free energy, and the interface carries no energy. Their numerical schemes are tied to their free energies: phase-field schemes break down when the interface energy is set to zero, and reactive diffusion codes rely on finite differences. We derive, from the thermodynamic extremal principle, a single finite element scheme that covers both limits: the stationarity of the Rayleighian functional (free energy rate plus one half of the dissipation, with mass conservation imposed by multipliers) with respect to the rates, fluxes and multipliers at a frozen state. Fluxes and chemical affinities are primary unknowns, so no derivative of the affinity is required. The time-discrete scheme is the corresponding incremental minimization; it conserves mass exactly and satisfies a discrete energy-dissipation inequality for every convex molar free energy, including the convex hull without regularization. We make explicit that this last case is a degenerate parabolic problem of Stefan type, whose degeneracy can be removed, without altering the free energy, only by a moving mesh; since our aim is the coupling to continuum mechanics and damage on a fixed mesh, we operate at the boundary of degeneracy and show that mass conservation, the energy balance and the second law remain intact there. Thermodynamic consistency is proved for multi-component systems, a scheme relating Onsager and diffusion coefficients is proposed, and the role of interface energy is studied in binary and ternary examples, the latter with vacancies as a non-conserved component.
item.dc:creator: Wolfgang Flachberger, Thomas Antretter, Swaroop Gaddikere-Nagaraja, Silvia Leitner, Manuel Petersmann, Jiri Svoboda

item.title: Numerical approximation of nonlinear fourth-order SPDEs with additive space-time white noise
item.description: arXiv:2501.18240v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the strong numerical approximation for a fourth-order stochastic nonlinear SPDE driven by space-time white noise on {{$d=1,2,3$}}-dimensional torus. We consider its full discretisation with a spectral Galerkin scheme in space and Euler scheme in time. We show the convergence with almost spatial rate $2-\frac{d}{2}$ and $\frac{6-d}{4} \wedge 1$-temporal rate obtained mainly via \it{Stochastic Sewing} technique.
item.dc:creator: Dirk Bl\"omker, Chengcheng Ling, Johannes Rimmele

item.title: A PINNs approach for the computation of eigenvalues in elliptic problems
item.description: arXiv:2507.03126v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we propose a method for computing eigenvalues of elliptic problems using Deep Learning techniques. A key feature of our approach is that it is independent of the space dimension and can compute arbitrary eigenvalues without requiring the prior computation of lower ones. Moreover, the method can be easily adapted to handle nonlinear eigenvalue problems.
item.dc:creator: Julian Fernandez Bonder, Ariel M. Salort

item.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo integration over $\mathbb{R}^s$ with boundary-damping importance sampling
item.description: arXiv:2509.07509v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper proposes a new importance sampling (IS) method tailored to quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) integration over $\mathbb{R}^s$. IS introduces a multiplicative weight that compensates for sampling from a proposal distribution rather than the target distribution. An unsuitable proposal, however, can yield an integrand that exhibits severe boundary growth and suffers from the curse of dimensionality, thus degrading QMC performance. Our approach is to design a weight function with the desired regularity and then construct a transport map realizing it as an IS proposal, thereby obtaining a transformed integrand amenable to QMC integration. We provide a rigorous analysis based on Fourier coefficients and apply it to lattice rule integration. Under suitable conditions, the proposed estimator achieves a fast convergence rate independent of the dimension $s$, making it suitable for high-dimensional problems.
item.dc:creator: Zexin Pan, Du Ouyang, Zhijian He

item.title: Solving the BGK Model and Boltzmann equation by Fourier Neural Operator with conservative constraints
item.description: arXiv:2510.13047v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The numerical approximation of the Boltzmann collision operator presents significant challenges because of its high dimensionality, quadratic nonlinearity, and nonlocal integral structure. In this work, we develop a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO)-based framework for learning finite time evolution operators associated with the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation and its simplified BGK model in different velocity space dimensions. The framework learns mappings between distribution functions in either sequence-to-sequence or point-to-point form and, once trained, enables rapid evaluation without repeated classical time evolution. To improve physical consistency, we introduce a conservative FNO (C-FNO) by augmenting the training loss with soft penalties for deviations in mass, momentum, and energy from the conservation law. Several numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate that the learned operators accurately reproduce the principal collision dynamics, while C-FNO generally reduces macroscopic drift relative to the standard FNO, highlighting its potential as a promising framework for physics-constrained operator learning in kinetic theory and other nonlinear integro-differential equations.
item.dc:creator: Boyun Hu, Kunlun Qi

item.title: Low-order CR--RT equilibrated-flux certification for semilinear problems on anisotropic meshes
item.description: arXiv:2602.01636v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a posteriori certification of semilinear diffusion--reaction problems on anisotropic simplicial meshes. Given a conforming finite element approximation, we bound its dual-norm residual by solving an auxiliary Crouzeix--Raviart problem and reconstructing an equilibrated Raviart--Thomas flux. Together with a coercivity estimate and a local derivative-Lipschitz bound, this gives a Newton--Kantorovich test for existence and local uniqueness in a computable energy-norm ball. We then use the verified radius to bound volume-type quantities of interest. The adjoint estimate accounts for the primal and adjoint residuals and retains explicit Taylor remainders for the nonlinear equation and, where relevant, the output functional. We also prove a conditional flux-mismatch consistency result on anisotropic mesh families. The CR--RT reconstruction and adjoint identities are established tools; here they provide a concrete low-order route to nonlinear solution and output certification. Numerical tests illustrate the bounds, but their double-precision evaluation does not constitute an interval-verified computation.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Ishizaka

item.title: A Reduced Order Model for First-Principles Atomistic Simulations
item.description: arXiv:2602.22390v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To leverage the redundancy between the electronic structure computed for various model parameters such as varying atomic positions, we present a data-driven modeling framework for Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory that bypasses the explicit optimization of electronic wavefunctions. We sample \textit{a priori} representative atomic configurations and construct a low-dimensional basis that efficiently approximates the electronic structure subspace. Subsequently, we employ this reduced basis in an iterative solver for the electronic single particle density matrix, thereby enabling the efficient determination of ground state without iterative wavefunction optimization. We demonstrate the accuracy of our approach in a Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics of a water molecule, showing that the resulting simulations accurately reproduce key structural properties, such as bond lengths and bond angle, obtained from full first-principles molecular dynamics. This work highlights the potential of data-driven approaches to develop low-dimensional electronic structure representations for first-principles simulations.
item.dc:creator: Siu Wun Cheung, Youngsoo Choi, Jonas Kaufman, Daniel Osei-Kuffuor, Jean-Luc Fattebert

item.title: A limiter-based approach to construct high-order fully-discrete entropy stable explicit DG schemes for hyperbolic conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2603.27478v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a class of novel high-order fully-discrete entropy stable (ES) discontinuous Galerkin (DG) schemes with explicit time discretization. The proposed methodology exploits a critical observation from [4] that the cell averages of classical DG solutions with forward Euler time stepping satisfy an ``entropy-stable-like'' property. Building on this result, fully-discrete entropy stability is rigorously enforced through a simple Zhang--Shu-type scaling limiter [65] applied as a post-processing step, without modifying the underlying spatial discretization. Furthermore, the proposed methodology can simultaneously enforce multiple discrete cell entropy inequalities, a capability unavailable in existing ES DG schemes. High-order accuracy in time is achieved by using strong-stability-preserving multistep methods. Theoretically, we prove that the proposed scheme indeed maintains high-order accuracy and establish a Lax--Wendroff-type theorem showing that the limit of the numerical solutions, if it exists, satisfies the desired entropy inequality. Extensive numerical tests for scalar equations and systems, including the nonconvex Buckley--Leverett problem and extreme examples of Euler equations, demonstrate optimal accuracy, enforcement of multiple entropy conditions, and strong robustness.
item.dc:creator: Yuchang Liu, Wei Guo, Yan Jiang, Zheng Sun

item.title: Global Convergence for an n-Dimensional Coefficient Inverse Problem for a Wave-Like Equation with a Single Location of the Point Source
item.description: arXiv:2603.27729v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, the first globally convergent numerical method is developed for an $n-$Dimensional coefficient inverse problem for a wave-like equation with the unknown potential in the most challenging case when the Dirac $% \delta -$ function is present in one of initial conditions for that equation and only a single location of the point source is used. Based on a Carleman estimate, convergence analysis is carried out. This analysis ensures the global convergence of the proposed numerical method, i.e. its convergence to the true solution is rigorously guaranteed regardless on the availabilty of a good first guess about this solution. A certain uniqueness theorem is proven as well. Extensive computational experiments with noisy data for both 2-Dimensional and 3-Dimensional cases demonstrate a high reconstruction accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Michael V. Klibanov, Jingzhi Li, Tian Niu, Vladimir G. Romanov

item.title: Deterministic sketching for Krylov subspace methods
item.description: arXiv:2604.07158v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Randomized sketching is currently introduced into every area of numerical linear algebra. In Krylov subspace methods, it allows runtime savings at the cost of small accuracy reductions. This work offers a different view on sketching in Krylov subspace methods by analyzing what subspace embeddings are obtained by arbitrary sketching matrices. The analysis gives rise to a deterministic sketching approach leveraging row subset selection techniques that yield subspace embeddings holding with probability 1. We propose deterministically sketched Krylov subspace methods for matrix functions, linear systems, and eigenvalue problems that show a similar performance to their randomly sketched counterparts.
item.dc:creator: Kai Bergermann

item.title: Efficient TV regularization of large-scale linear inverse problems via the SCD semismooth* Newton method with applications in tomography
item.description: arXiv:2605.12041v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider the efficient numerical minimization of Tikhonov functionals resulting from total-variation (TV) regularization of linear inverse problems. Since the TV penalty is non-smooth, this is typically done either via smooth approximations, which are inexact, or using non-smooth optimization techniques, which can often be numerically expensive, in particular for large-scale problems. Here, we present a numerically efficient minimization approach based on the recently proposed semismooth* Newton method, which employs a novel concept of graphical derivatives and exhibits locally superlinear convergence. The proposed approach is specifically tailored to TV regularization, suitable for large-scale inverse problems, and supported by strong mathematical convergence guarantees. Furthermore, we demonstrate its performance on two (large-scale) tomographic imaging problems and compare our results to those obtained via other state-of-the-art TV regularization approaches. Finally, an open-source Matlab implementation of the proposed method is made available online at https://github.com/HGfrerer/TVReg-2D-Semismoothstar-Newton.
item.dc:creator: Helmut Gfrerer, Simon Hubmer, Stefan Kindermann, Jaakko Kultima, Ronny Ramlau, Tanja Tarvainen

item.title: When can a neural operator replace a coarse solve? Architectural principles for two-level preconditioning
item.description: arXiv:2605.19867v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Neural operators are increasingly used as accelerators inside classical numerical methods, but it is rarely clear which architectural ingredients matter for which application. We answer this question for one important use case: the coarse-space correction inside a two-level preconditioner for discretised linear partial differential equations. We systematically vary four DeepONet-like architectures along two design axes: input discretisation (sampling versus integration against a basis) and source-term linearity. In doing this, we show that the favourable corner of this 2x2 design is occupied by a single architecture, the Neural Green's Operator (NGO), and that moving away from it produces predictable failure modes: highly non-normal preconditioned systems, breakdown of preconditioned conjugate gradients on self-adjoint problems, and stagnation on non-self-adjoint ones. Used as a coarse-space correction, the NGO matches the iteration count of an exact coarse solve on 2D diffusion and advection-diffusion problems. The principle generalises: integrating inputs against the basis used for the output is what allows a neural operator to serve as a Galerkin-type coarse-space correction.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Melchers, Victorita Dolean, Michael Abdelmalik

item.title: Hybrid Analog-Digital Approximate Inverse Preconditioning for Krylov Methods
item.description: arXiv:2606.17227v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Analog in-memory computing enables highly parallel matrix-vector multiplications with reduced data movement, but the resulting operations are noisy, quantized, and affected by device- and circuit-level non-idealities. This paper studies approximate inverse preconditioning for Krylov subspace methods in a hybrid analog-digital architecture that combines a conventional digital processor with an analog in-memory computing (AIMC) unit. The digital host performs sparse products with the coefficient matrix and the precision-sensitive Krylov operations, while the AIMC unit performs preconditioner applications through analog crossbar matrix-vector multiplications. Since the realized preconditioner is inexact and application-dependent, the outer iteration is formulated as the flexible GMRES method. We show that analog execution changes the usual preconditioner design problem in the sense that a stronger digital preconditioner may be less effective after analog scaling, write noise, input/output perturbations, quantization, and clipping are taken into account. We use exact block inverses and sparse approximate inverses as reference constructions and develop a noise-matching criterion for Monte Carlo approximate inverse (MCAI) construction. We also study damping and nesting to improve robustness. Numerical experiments, in which analog matrix-vector products are simulated rather than executed on hardware, show that analog-aware choices of block size, damping, MCAI construction accuracy, and nesting are important for robust convergence.
item.dc:creator: Shikhar Shah, Rui Peng Li, Tayfun Gokmen, Vassilis Kalantzis, Lior Horesh, Yuanzhe Xi

item.title: Numerical analysis of the Biot equations coupled to frictional contact mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2607.02030v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a mathematical model of a poroviscoelastic medium subject to frictional contact with a rigid obstacle, and study its numerical approximation. This model couples the Biot equations and contact conditions in the form of normal compliance and Coulomb friction. The resulting variational problem consists of a linear partial differential equation coupled to a nonlinear variational inequality. We propose and analyze a fully discrete numerical scheme for this problem, using conformal finite elements in space and the implicit Euler method in time. Existence and uniqueness of the discrete solution is established, and stability and a priori error estimates are derived. A numerical experiment is performed in which numerical error estimates are computed and compared to the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Marius Nevland, Kundan Kumar, Inga Berre, Jakub Wiktor Both, Eirik Keilegavlen

item.title: Fixed-grid symmetry defects and order recovery for explicit Laplace--rotation integrators in Bose--Einstein dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.07923v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A factorization exact for the continuous Laplace--rotation flow need not preserve time symmetry when implemented stage by stage on a Fourier grid. We analyze two explicit exact integrators (EEIs) for rotating Bose--Einstein condensates. For the seven-factor EEI, a constant-state Fourier coefficient proves that its fixed-grid logarithm has a nonzero quadratic defect on every centered even grid for any nonzero rotation vector. For a distinct five-operator EEI, a nonconstant-mode certificate proves the same obstruction on nonsingular coefficient branches whenever at least two rotation components are nonzero. In real-coefficient compact splitting, merging adjacent linear stages with fractions $c_j$ multiplies either defect by the strictly positive factor $\kappa=\sum_jc_j^2$; nominal high order therefore cannot be guaranteed uniformly at fixed grid. For the seven-factor implementation, the accumulated-response formula predicts $\kappa_4/\kappa_6\approx0.7606$ for nominal fourth- and sixth-order compact schemes (CS4/CS6). Scalar dipolar and spin-1 tests of that implementation verify the predicted amplitude ratio and reveal a crossover toward first-order compact behavior under time refinement. Pairing a forward linear half-step with its method adjoint around the exact nonlinear flow restores symmetry of the complete step; classical compositions then recover fourth and sixth order at fixed grid. The analysis provides explicit structural diagnostics and a direct structure-preserving repair.
item.dc:creator: Tianqi Zhang, Fei Xue

item.title: Analysis of the Virtual Element Approximation for the Smagorinsky Model
item.description: arXiv:2609.02433v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider the Smagorinsky model for the Navier-Stokes equations within a virtual element framework. Under the standard assumption of small data, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a solution. Assuming more regularity to the solutions, we derive the known \del{suboptimal} convergence rates $h$, using $k>1$, for the a priori error estimates of the Smagorinsky model in two dimensional domains. We additionally prove that divergence-free virtual discretizations provide improved convergence orders, with weaker regularity assumptions than in the finite element literature. We conclude the paper with numerical results that corroborate the theory.
item.dc:creator: Karol L. Cascavita, Francesca Marcon, Maria Strazzullo

item.title: Multiscale and stability analysis of an Aw-Rascle-Zhang-type model with driver-dependent acceleration
item.description: arXiv:2609.15934v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new traffic flow model. The main idea is to describe acceleration effects in the Aw-Rascle-Zhang model through an additional driver-dependent equation, thereby allowing individual driver characteristics to evolve dynamically rather than being prescribed solely by the traffic density. The resulting system provides a hyperbolic description of traffic dynamics and admits an explicit analysis of its characteristic structure, Riemann problem, and entropy properties. To investigate the stability of the proposed model, we perform a Chapman-Enskog expansion up to second order and derive the corresponding diffusive and higher-order corrections. This analysis reveals how the stability properties depend on the underlying velocity and pressure functions. Several examples are presented to illustrate the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Gerster, Giuseppe Visconti

item.title: Backward log orthogonal functions and their approximation theory
item.description: arXiv:2609.20901v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new class of backward logarithmic orthogonal functions and generalized backward logarithmic orthogonal functions, constructed by applying a terminal-endpoint logarithmic mapping to generalized Laguerre polynomials. These functions are designed for backward spectral approximations of problems whose solutions exhibit weak singularities at the terminal endpoint. The proposed basis functions generate non-polynomial weighted approximation spaces with nodes naturally clustered near the singular endpoint, and therefore provide an effective framework for resolving algebraic and logarithmic endpoint singularities. We develop the basic approximation theory for these backward logarithmic orthogonal functions, including recurrence relations, derivative formulas, orthogonality, Sturm--Liouville characterization, mapped Laguerre--Gauss quadrature rules, weighted projection estimates, backward Lagrange interpolation estimates, inverse inequalities, and stability properties in weighted Sobolev-type spaces defined through a terminal logarithmic pseudo-derivative. A generalized version of the basis is also introduced by incorporating an algebraic scaling parameter, which improves the flexibility of the approximation space and allows singular factors to be represented more effectively. The error analysis and numerical results show that the proposed backward logarithmic basis is particularly suitable for weakly regular functions with terminal-endpoint singularities and can recover exponential or high-order convergence rates that are typically lost when usual polynomial approximations are applied directly.
item.dc:creator: Mahmoud A. Zaky

item.title: Numerical Realization of an Entropy-Based Selection Principle in the Example of Kelvin-Helmholtz Instability
item.description: arXiv:2609.24479v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we extend numerical schemes based on parameterized Young measures and linear programming to two space dimensions and apply them to the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability governed by the two-dimensional Euler equations of gas dynamics. We construct first-, second-, third-, fifth-, seventh-, and ninth-order Young-measure schemes and compare them with corresponding standard local Lax-Friedrichs (LLF) flux-splitting schemes and LLF schemes equipped with an entropy-based local characteristic decomposition (LLF-ELCD). We examine instantaneous and time-averaged density profiles, cumulative averages across spatial reconstruction orders, regional empirical density distributions, averaged density marginals, and several selection criteria for dissipative weak solutions. The numerical results reveal scheme-dependent flow patterns, particularly in the small-scale structures generated during the roll-up of the shear layers. At every reconstruction order considered, the Young-measure schemes yield the largest time-averaged physical entropy. By contrast, the LLF-ELCD schemes do not systematically yield larger entropy than the standard LLF schemes and therefore do not constitute a consistent maximum-entropy selection mechanism. The averaged density marginals of the Young measures are concentrated on several neighboring density states, and the later cumulative averages are closer for all Young-measure schemes. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the two-dimensional Young-measure formulation and show that the objective function in the linear-programming problem can act as an effective selection mechanism. The observed entropy preference is consistent with the local optimization of the expected physical entropy. It cannot be reproduced by merely incorporating entropy into a conventional numerical construction.
item.dc:creator: Shaoshuai Chu, Michael Herty

item.title: BDF2-type integrator for Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation in micromagnetics: IMEX time-stepping and full effective field
item.description: arXiv:2610.10291v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the BDF2-type finite-element integrator proposed in [M. Ald\'e, M. Feischl, D. Praetorius; BDF2-type integrator for Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation in micromagnetics: unconditional weak convergence to weak solutions. (Math. Comp., 2026, doi:10.1090/mcom/4210)] to the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation with lower-order effective-field contributions and current-induced non-conservative torques arising in micromagnetic applications. To incorporate these additional terms while retaining a linear solve at each time step, we employ an implicit-explicit (IMEX) time splitting. Our main theorem proves unconditional weak convergence of the fully discrete approximations towards weak solutions of the LLG equation. The analysis removes the mild but artificial CFL-type restrictions required at the first and final time steps in [Ald\'e M., Feischl M., Praetorius D.; Math. Comp., 2026]. Furthermore, in the presence of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), the convergence is likewise unconditional and does not require the CFL-type restriction imposed in [G. Hrkac, C.-M. Pfeiler, D. Praetorius, M. Ruggeri, A. Segatti, and B. Stiftner. Convergent tangent plane integrators for the simulation of chiral magnetic skyrmion dynamics. (Adv. Comput. Math., 2019. doi: 10.1007/s10444-019-09667-z)]. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings.
item.dc:creator: Michele Ald\'e, Dirk Praetorius, Agus L. Soenjaya

item.title: Emulating the Darcy Solution Operator by Heat-Semigroup Functional Calculus and Pointwise Products
item.description:
arXiv:2610.20106v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We approximate the Darcy solution operator $(a,f)\mapsto u$, where $-\operatorname{div}(a
abla u)=f$, by operator networks built only from heat-semigroup evaluations $e^{-tL_0}$ of a single fixed reference operator and pointwise products. The key obstacle is the variable-coefficient coupling $
abla a\cdot
abla u$. We show that it is produced by the heat product defect $[P_t(bu)-P_tb\,P_tu]/(2t)$, which converges quantitatively to $
abla b\cdot
abla u$. Inserted into a Laplacian-preconditioned Richardson iteration, this yields an explicit scheme of depth $O(\log(1/\varepsilon)/\log(1/q))$ whose $\dot H^1$ error is at most $\varepsilon$, uniformly over the coefficient class and $L^2$ data, with all parameters explicit. Each block is controlled in continuum operator norm, without Galerkin truncation. On the torus, band-limited inputs admit an exact pseudo-spectral realization on a grid of $O(1/(\varepsilon a_{\min}))$ points per direction, up to logarithmic and class-dependent factors. The argument extends by carre du champ calculus to strongly local Dirichlet spaces with a spectral gap and a Bakry--Emery bound $\mathrm{BE}(-K,\infty)$, with dimension-independent constants after spectral-gap normalization. On the torus we also obtain a $C^2$-type coefficient class and a refinement to Wiener classes of regularity $1+	heta$, with product-defect rate $t^{	heta/2}$. The factor $1/(2t)$ makes the proved scheme ill-conditioned at small $\varepsilon$.
item.dc:creator: Dawid Hanrahan

item.title: A Givens-Based Direct Eigenvalue Swapping Algorithm with Rounding Error Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.30795v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a given matrix $ A $ in the real Schur form, the eigenvalue swapping algorithm is used to swap two adjacent diagonal blocks. In LAPACK, this operation is performed by the subroutine xLAEXC, which is based on a direct swapping algorithm proposed by Bai and Demmel in 1993. In this work, we propose a modified direct swapping algorithm for two $ 2 \times 2 $ blocks, replacing Householder QR with a pivoted Givens QR factorization. A thorough error analysis shows that the modified algorithm can achieve an error bound of the form $ O( \boldsymbol{u} \lVert A \rVert ) $ under mild assumptions, where $ \boldsymbol{u} $ is the unit roundoff. We present empirical evidence to illustrate the superior stability of our algorithm over existing approaches.
item.dc:creator: Meiyue Shao, Rentao Xu

item.title: Multivariate Lebesgue Bounds for Leja-type Lower Grids
item.description: arXiv:2610.40177v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish algebraic upper bounds for the Lebesgue constants of multivariate polynomial interpolation on Leja-type lower grids in terms of the total number of nodes $N$. For fixed dimension $d\geq2$, write $q_d=d/(d-1)$. Disk Leja grids and their images under exterior conformal maps that extend holomorphically and injectively across the unit circle share the bound $O(N^{\delta_d})$, with $\delta_d=\tfrac12+q_d^{-1}\log_2(1+2^{q_d/2})$. This gives $\delta_2\approx1.292481$ in two dimensions and $\delta_3\approx1.448799$ in three dimensions. For $\mathfrak R$-Leja grids, we obtain $O(N^{\beta_d})$ with $\beta_d=1+q_d^{-1}\log_2(1+2^{q_d})$, which gives $\beta_2\approx2.160964$ and $\beta_3\approx2.291168$. Both bounds hold uniformly over all finite lower sets and choices of disk Leja sequences, with constants depending only on the dimension and the conformal maps.
item.dc:creator: Phil-Alexander Hofmann, Michael Hecht

item.title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for high-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
item.description: arXiv:2611.14041v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The time to solution of an iterative solver depends on the number of iterations and the cost per iteration. This paper develops algorithms that reduce both for elliptic problems discretized with high-order continuous finite elements on distributed GPUs, implemented in a unified matrix-free code supporting CUDA, HIP and SYCL. A distributed direct fast-diagonalization (FD) Poisson solver provides exact solutions on tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate direction. Its tensor data remain distributed, moved between slab layouts using collective transposes or kept in place by a Schur-complement approach. A two-level hybrid Schwarz preconditioner with FD cell solves (HS-FD) is extended to 2:1 hanging-node octrees with exact local cell inverses, while a p-multigrid preconditioner with Chebyshev--Jacobi smoothing (CJ-pMG) resolves hanging-node constraints at every level within fused kernels. Both approaches exploit FP32, where cell shapes and coefficients allow, within an FP64 conjugate-gradient iteration, adaptively select replicated or distributed coarse levels, support block solves for multiple right-hand sides and determine all parameters from the operator without case-specific tuning. Comparisons with Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradients (Jacobi PCG), MFEM, nekRS and deal.II span uniform, graded and octree meshes, layered coefficients, and four applications across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs. The direct solver is two to three orders of magnitude faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes. HS-FD converges in 11 iterations for the generalised Poisson problem on octree meshes across 8 to 1024 MI250X graphics compute dies. These results provide practical guidelines for solver selection based on mesh structure and coefficient characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Gourab Panigrahi, Phani Motamarri

item.title: Model Order Reduction for Quantum Molecular Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2509.07340v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum molecular dynamics (QMD) provides a high-fidelity physical framework for modeling atomic and molecular phenomena from first principles. However, its mathematical formulation requires solving iterative, high-dimensional electronic structure problems at every physical state step. Within the broader data-driven computational mechanics paradigm, we present a projection-based model order reduction framework for electronic structure calculation in QMD. By discovering a low-dimensional manifold of the electronic solution space within Kohn-Sham density functional theory, our approach projects the governing variational formulation onto an intrinsically reduced subspace. This avoids full-space iterative wavefunction optimization while preserving rigorous physical symmetries and state consistency. We demonstrate this methodology on a water molecule, demonstrating strong agreement with high-fidelity reference solutions across structural trajectories and thermodynamic observables through canonical coordinate alignment and structured manifold sampling.
item.dc:creator: Siu Wun Cheung, Youngsoo Choi, Jean-Luc Fattebert, Daniel Osei-Kuffuor

item.title: Evaluation of External Magnetic Flux Density in Piezo-Flexomagnetic Nanobeams Using a Hybrid 1D-2D Finite Element Framework
item.description: arXiv:2605.19422v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Most theoretical models of piezo-flexomagnetic nanostructures forcibly impose magnetic isolation at the structure-air interface, neglecting the external magnetic domain entirely. This mathematical compromise limits the model's capability to account for stray-field behavior in non-contact applications. To overcome this gap, our study proposes a fully coupled hybrid finite element formulation combining a 1D Timoshenko beam model with a 2D magneto-static problem, encompassing both the beam body and the surrounding air domain. By continuously mapping 1D structural kinematics into the 2D space to define the mechanically induced magnetic flux, and subsequently integrating the resulting 2D scalar potential back into 1D static generalized magnetic loads, this framework enhances the capability of the simple 1D beam model. The results present the distribution of an external magnetic flux in piezo-flexomagnetic structures and identify the material parameters driving this. Ultimately, the proposed computational method extends the boundary of a 1D beam model to an infinite-domain multiphysics environment.
item.dc:creator: Lala Samprit Ray, Bishweshwar Babu

item.title: Global existence, blow-up behavior and numerical simulations for a class of chemotaxis-driven fish-mussel systems
item.description: arXiv:2606.18695v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we investigate a chemotaxis-driven fish--mussel ecosystem model described by a coupled system of partial differential equations subject to homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. Under suitable assumptions on the system parameters and initial data, we establish the global existence of classical solutions by employing semigroup methods together with a priori estimates. We also examine the possible blow-up behavior of solutions in a three-dimensional domain. To support the theoretical analysis, a finite element method is developed for the numerical approximation of the system, and convergence studies based on mesh refinement are carried out to verify the accuracy and stability of the proposed numerical scheme. Furthermore, numerical simulations illustrating the blow-up behavior of solutions in the computational domain are presented.
item.dc:creator: Gnanasekaran Shanmugasundaram, Jitraj Saha

item.title: Filon Methods for Highly Oscillatory Controlled Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.13580v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fast and accurate classical simulation of quantum systems is a central challenge in the design and control of quantum computers, but the highly oscillatory dynamics of these systems severely limit the efficiency of standard numerical methods. To address this, we adapt Filon quadrature for oscillatory integrals into two numerical methods, called Filon and Controlled Filon, for solving linear systems of ODEs with highly oscillatory solutions. We tailor both methods for efficient implementation in controlled quantum systems, and the Controlled Filon method additionally accounts for the oscillatory structure of the control pulses. We show by numerical experiments that these methods significantly reduce the computational cost of accurately simulating systems of superconducting transmon qubits by decreasing the number of timesteps needed to reach a given level of precision, with only a modest increase in the cost per timestep. For a realistic simulation of the dynamics of a CNOT gate, the Controlled Filon method is the most efficient method tested at every target accuracy, outperforming the best Hermite method by up to 6x and the Hermite method of the same order by up to 500x.
item.dc:creator: Spencer Lee, Daniel Appel\"o

item.title: Learning to Solve Stochastic Controls with Unknown Drifts and Running Rewards: Theory, Algorithms and Convergence
item.description: arXiv:2609.14972v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study continuous-time and possibly high-dimensional stochastic control problems where drift coefficients and running reward functions are unknown. Due to these missing model primitives, we take the exploratory, reinforcement learning (RL) framework of Wang, Zariphopoulou, and Zhou(2020) with relaxed controls and entropy regularization. The objective is to develop theoretically grounded, efficient and scalable RL algorithms to learn both the optimal value functions (which also solve the exploratory HJB equation) and optimal exploratory feedback control policies. When the diffusion coefficients do not contain control, we employ probabilistic representations of both the optimal value function and its gradient based on an auxiliary state process depending only on the diffusion part of the original dynamics. With a delicate analysis on some properly defined mappings and their fixed points, this leads to the introduction of our policy iteration algorithms and their convergence. We demonstrate the performance of our algorithms through various numerical examples. Finally, we study a special control-dependent diffusion case where probability representation of the Hessian is called for.
item.dc:creator: Jin Ma, Gaozhan Wang, Jianfeng Zhang, Xunyu Zhou

item.title: An energy-stable and accuracy-preserving finite volume scheme for wall-distance computations
item.description: arXiv:2609.16885v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The distance to the nearest wall provides a length scale in models of wall-bounded turbulence. Computing this distance accurately on highly stretched meshes is challenging because small near-wall cells restrict explicit pseudo-time steps and geometric singularities can induce spurious oscillations. To address these challenges, this paper presents a semi-implicit finite-volume scheme based on a scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) for solving the pseudo-time Eikonal equation on unstructured meshes. An upwind weighted least-squares reconstruction supplies the gradients used to evaluate the cell-averaged Eikonal residuals. The artificial-viscosity term is discretized using a two-point face flux whose coefficient vanishes as the regularized residuals in both adjacent cells tend to zero. The SAV update advances the semi-discrete system in pseudo-time by evaluating the residuals and viscosity coefficients explicitly and coupling the wall-distance averages and auxiliary variables implicitly. The analysis establishes unconditional energy stability under homogeneous Dirichlet conditions, permitting a grid-independent global pseudo-time step. The system's M-matrix structure guarantees nonnegative cell averages of the physical wall distance under a separate step restriction, while residual regularization and artificial viscosity preserve the formal order of spatial accuracy. Numerical tests confirm second-order spatial convergence for the quarter-cylinder case and demonstrate robust wall-distance computation on highly stretched meshes typical of Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes simulations. The SAV formulation is independent of the reconstruction scheme, providing a basis for extensions to higher-order finite-volume methods and other nonconservative scalar equations.
item.dc:creator: Xiaorui Xu, Qian Wang

item.title: Towards Exact Multidimensional Fluxes: A Structure-Preserving Data-Informed Framework for Riemann Solvers
item.description: arXiv:2610.35265v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Finite volume and discontinuous Galerkin methods evolve the discrete solution using space-time flux integrals over mesh faces, which typically depend on solutions to local Riemann problems. In the multidimensional Riemann problem setting, this integral is difficult to evaluate exactly because of complex wave interactions. In this work, we show that the exact space-time flux integral is a polynomial in the time step and face dimensions. This motivates a learning-based approach, as only the mapping from the initial states to the polynomial coefficients needs to be learned. We propose a structure-preserving, data-informed Riemann solver framework that uses a neural network trained on high-resolution simulation data to learn this mapping. Key structural properties, including consistency and mirror symmetry, are enforced by construction. Provided that the high-resolution simulations converge to the exact flux integrals and the network accurately predicts the coefficients, this framework yields near-exact flux integrals for use in numerical simulations. We demonstrate the framework using classical implosion and explosion problems for the two-dimensional Euler equations. In an unsplit MUSCL-Hancock scheme, the learned Riemann solver remains stable at a CFL number of 0.9, whereas the same scheme using the exact one-dimensional Riemann solver fails. Compared with the latter scheme at CFL=0.45, the learned scheme is slightly more accurate and requires approximately 30% less computational time.
item.dc:creator: Yucheng Zhang, Clint Dawson

item.title: Linearize or Discretize First? Error Estimates under Mesh-Uniform Regularity and Exponential Stability for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2610.39269v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation, and its spatial semidiscretization by a weighted cubic Hermite Galerkin method. A small nonlinear wave can be approximated by a linear discrete simulation in two orders: linearize first and then discretize, or discretize first and then linearize. Both orders lead to the same total error. They divide this error differently between linearization and discretization. The difference of the two divisions is what we call the ordering error. We show that it is quadratic in the size of the initial datum and carries a positive power of the mesh size, for all time. It can be used to assess the effect of a coarse-mesh correction for nonlinear problems. For the continuous problem, the solution map is analytic, and the semigroup of the linearized equation has Crandall-Pazy regularity with the exact index 3/2. For the weighted scheme, the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit exponential stability, Kato smoothing and Crandall-Pazy regularity, with bounds uniform in the mesh size. The nonlinear solution maps are analytic, also uniformly in the mesh size. These properties give error estimates in which the error and the datum are measured in the same norm: in the energy norm, in $H_0^1$ and in $H^2$. On every interval $[t_0,\infty)$, $t_0>0$, same-norm convergence holds uniformly on balls at algebraic rates. The ordering error is of order $h^{1/6}$ times the square of the energy norm of the datum, uniformly for all $t\ge0$.
item.dc:creator: Kangsheng Liu

item.title: Ignoring Blow-Ups for Approximations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08208v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is well known that for SDEs with non-Lipschitz coefficients, the Euler scheme can fail to converge in an Lp sense. It is also widely observed that convergence fails only due to rare explosive trajectories, that distort the expectation. In this work we demonstrate that almost any method of removing these rare explosive trajectories leads to convergence in a suitable strong and weak sense. We apply this framework to coefficients that grow faster than linearly at infinity and Lennard-Jones type coefficients that explode like a reciprocal power on a compact set.
item.dc:creator: Tim Johnston
